rationale: This is essentially the archive's best signal with one term added to the denominator, and the change is not innocuous — putting five-year capex in the denominator makes the "purchased share" mechanically decreasing in capital intensity, so the long leg tilts toward high-capex firms, directly opposing the investment-discipline direction the rest of the archive establishes and confounding the coverage gain with a new sector/capital-intensity exposure.

Despite the disclaimer, this is an averaging of the archive's two top-performing signals whose legs (purchased share of growth budget and count of acquisition years) are near-mechanically correlated, so it will almost certainly land between them and teach nothing about mechanism, with the arbitrary 1:2 nested-SUMRANK weighting adding a free parameter rather than an economic hypothesis.

The self-accumulated-versus-purchased intangible comparison is a genuinely new and well-motivated framing of the accounting-mismeasurement story, though the R&D-to-assets leg risks reducing the result to the well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly and the absence of industry neutralization is a known weakness in this exact channel given the archive's earlier tangibility results.

This is a near-monotone reparameterization of the already-tested industry_neutral_built_versus_bought_stock (difference of intan/at and ppent/at recast as intan/(intan+ppent), same industry z-score, same cash-profit leg), i.e. a cosmetic deflator change to an evaluated signal rather than a new mechanism.

Replacing the raw asset-scaled acquisition intensity with the bounded purchased share is a defensible, specifically diagnosed fix to the weak Fama-MacBeth slope of the earlier failed-acquirer short, but the test should be interpreted cautiously since the three-year cash-flow-change leg is itself a strong standalone predictor and may carry most of the alpha.

Testing a change in the bounded allocation mix across non-overlapping windows is a substantively different (level versus transition) question and is properly motivated by why the raw-intensity version failed, though the share degenerates to a noisy 0/1 flip for non-R&D firms and is undefined for firms doing neither, so coverage and composition stability need checking before any positive result is believed.
